title: "Word Splitting and Pathname Expansion"

# Word Splitting and Pathname Expansion

After parameter expansion and command substitution, Bash performs **Word Splitting** on unquoted words using the Internal Field Separator (`$IFS`). By default, `$IFS` is set to space, tab, and newline.

### The Dangers of Word Splitting

```bash
filename="My Important Document.pdf"

# DANGEROUS: Word splitting breaks filename into three arguments: "My", "Important", "Document.pdf"
rm $filename
# rm: cannot remove 'My': No such file or directory
# rm: cannot remove 'Important': No such file or directory
# rm: cannot remove 'Document.pdf': No such file or directory

# SAFE: Always double-quote variables
rm "$filename"
```

### Controlling Globbing (Pathname Expansion)

Globbing matches filesystem patterns. When no match is found, Bash's default behavior is to return the unexpanded pattern as literal text, which can cause subtle failures:

```bash
# Enable nullglob: unmatched globs expand to nothing instead of literal string
shopt -s nullglob

# Enable failglob: unmatched globs throw a hard error
shopt -s failglob

# Disable globbing entirely
set -f  # or set -o noglob
```
